newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Zinc prices continue to defy fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Zinc prices continue to defy fundamentals.

text.p: A concerted effort to force the London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc market higher in defiance of its fundamentals again met outstanding success on Thursday as prices set fresh 7 year peaks.
Most of the commodity market action on Wednesday was in the industrial and precious metals.

Traders said that with the Chinese zinc industry showing concern in China Metals magazine over a large short position established on the LME by a Chinese smelter it appeared a European merchant and investment funds on the other side of the market appeared to be gaining the upper hand.

The Zhuzhou smelter will have to buy back or roll forward its positions, if it can not cancel them out by delivering metal into LME warehouses by mid-September. It is this possibility that is pushing prices and premiums to fresh highs, traders said.
The premium for spot zinc metal on the LME rose to $40 a tonne over three months delivery which itself was at a seven year high around $1,560.
"We are seeing fresh highs and there is nothing to suggest the market should be sold off. The market is looking at $1,600." said Martin Squires, analyst at brokers Rudolf Wolff.

But Asian traders involved in physical business said they could see no fundamental improvement to support strong zinc prices while in Europe it was much the same story with the nearby premium and the summer holidays stifling physical market activity.
The aluminium market continued to edge higher as LME warehouse stocks fell again and a supply squeeze began to build during August delivery dates.

Traders said that although there was still around 640,000 tonnes of metal in warehouses, after Wednesday's 3,475 tonnes fall, it was believed that a large proportion was in strong hands and not readily available to the market.

The three months delivery aluminium price rose to around $1,650 before meeting investment fund selling and the spot metal discount narrowed into around $4 a tonne, from $20 at the start of the week, under the influence of the developing squeeze.

But the recent copper supply tightness was disappearing fast with the spot premium down to around $50 from $270 a tonne ten days ago. This has taken the benchmark three months delivery price below $2,300 although it was relatively steady today.
The recent rally in the gold price was hit by selling from funds and producers and this took the spot bullion price in London below $322 at one stage from above $328.00 an ounce on Wednesday.
